subject: Post-call: data jurisdiction, derivative data controls & failover constraints
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-02T09:15:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on data jurisdiction and retention

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Summary: ClearPath Health is evaluating Redwood for a patient-facing summarization feature. Primary requirements you flagged: (1) no patient-identifiable data leaves EU for processing without an authorized legal basis, (2) logs and retention must satisfy auditability for 1 year, (3) ability to run in a private VPC for production should be included in the SOW.

Actions we agreed on: 
1) We will provide a short matrix showing: where PII can be processed (EU pinning options), what data is considered derivative (embeddings, paraphrases) and retention defaults, and acceptable cross-region failover behavior.
2) We will attach a draft SLA and a compliance checklist for your security team.
3) Technical demo (private tenancy options) next Thursday — I’ll coordinate scheduling.

Two clarifying questions from our side to make the matrix prescriptive: 
- Can you confirm whether ClearPath considers derived embeddings and model outputs to be "patient-identifiable" by policy, or are those treated as pseudonymized artifacts? This affects retention and encryption-at-rest key handling.
- For cross-region failover, do you need synchronous replication of KV caches and logs, or would an asynchronous, read-only cold fallback to a US region for DR be acceptable if EU capacity is exhausted?

I’ve attached a first-pass checklist and the SLA draft for review. If helpful I can pull in Olivier from infra and your security contact to a short Q&A.

Thanks,
Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ClearPath-Data-Handling-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-draft-CPH.docx (doc)

From: Emma Lowe <emma@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearPath Health Security <security@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-02T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on data jurisdiction and retention

Thanks Monica — helpful recap. Quick answers and a couple of follow-ups from Security: 

- On derived artifacts: our policy today treats embeddings and generated summaries as potentially re-identifiable if they contain verbatim PHI. For low-risk outputs we can accept pseudonymized treatment, but anything that could be re-linked to a patient must be treated as PII. We will need an option to enforce redaction or masking before storage.
- Failover: primary requirement is no active processing of EU patient data outside the EU except in DR scenarios that are explicitly approved and logged. For DR we can accept an asynchronous cold fallback to a non-EU region provided it is documented, encrypted, and we have manual authorization step.

Security wants specifics on: audit log retention policy (minimum 12 months), ability to disable request logging at customer level for certain endpoints, and proof that keys for EU-pinned deployments are managed separately (KMS separation or HSM).

Can you send a binding statement on: (1) default log retention, (2) whether we can disable request bodies from being logged, and (3) how backup snapshots are geo-located? If you can’t provide binding language, point us to the section in your contract/SOC where these are covered.

Emma
Director, Product Security
ClearPath Health
emma@clearpathhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@clearpathhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on data jurisdiction and retention

Emma — thanks, this is very actionable. Technical clarifications below (also adding to the checklist PDF):

1) Classification: We treat "derived artifacts" (embeddings, cached prompts/results) as tenant data. If an output contains verbatim PHI, we surface that as tenant-owned PII and by default retain according to tenant settings. We can offer a preprocessing redaction hook (inline) that runs before any token is written to disk or cache.

2) Pinning + failover model: 
- EU pinning: we support strict region pinning (processing + primary KV cache + primary logs stored within the EU region).
- Cross-region failover: we support a manual-approval DR flow: if EU capacity is exhausted, Redwood can bring up a read-only failover in US-west for a predefined maintenance window. This flow requires (a) pre-authorization in the SOW, (b) activation via a documented runbook, and (c) that all persisted backups brought to US region are encrypted with a different key namespace (we track key provenance).

3) Logs and retention: by default request logs (metadata + full request/response bodies) are retained 90 days. We can offer a 12-month retention option as part of Dedicated/Private plans in contract. For hosted accounts, we can provide a toggle to redact request bodies from logs at the tenant level (metadata-only logging). Redaction is a configuration flag we can enforce before writing logs.

4) Backups & snapshots: Periodic snapshots are taken and stored in the same geo-region by default. Cross-region snapshots are only created for DR scenarios and are controlled by the backup policy in the SOW; cross-region snapshots are encrypted and tracked in our KMS audit trail.

I’m attaching a short technical appendix that maps these features to the checklist items. If you want HSM-level separation for EU keys, that’s available under our Private deployment option (we'll add that callout to the contract).

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

Attachments: Redwood-EU-pin-and-failover-summary.pdf (PDF)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lowe <emma@clearpathhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-03T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on data jurisdiction and retention

Emma — adding a couple of compliance/legal notes to Ben's excellent technical summary: 

- Binding language: Our SOC 2 and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) contain commitments around data location, encryption, and logging. For ClearPath we can include contract terms that specify: (1) EU-only processing except DR scenarios, (2) 12-month log retention for Dedicated/Private, and (3) tenant-controlled redaction for request bodies. We will annotate the DPA and add an explicit clause around manual DR authorization and key provenance for cross-region snapshots.

- Next steps I propose: 
  1) Monica to share a marked-up checklist with the Security team by EOD tomorrow.
  2) Redwood to produce a one-page binding statement (legal) that we can include in the SOW covering default log retention, body-redaction option, and backup geo-location.
  3) Schedule the private-tenancy demo for next Thursday (Monica will propose time slots).
  4) If Security agrees to the manual DR workflow, we can include DocuSign-ready SLA addendum in the deal and move to procurement.

I’ll draft the one-pager and circulate for internal review; Monica, Ben — can you review the language before I send it to Emma?

Vivek
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Emma Lowe <emma@clearpathhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-04T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying questions on data jurisdiction and retention

Team — this looks good and addresses our core concerns. A few final points before we loop procurement: 

- Please include an explicit sentence that request bodies will be redactable via tenant flag for our production account. That is non-negotiable for the initial rollout.
- For DR, the manual approval step and the audit trail showing key provenance are acceptable. We will want the runbook excerpt in the SOW.
- Confirm that the 12-month log retention option will be in the SOW for Dedicated and that we will not be charged hidden egress for cross-region DR snapshot transfer (call out in procurement).

If Redwood can provide the one-page binding statement and the annotated checklist, Security will circulate internally and we’ll aim to have procurement kickoff next week. Please send DocuSign when the SLA addendum is ready.

Thanks,
Emma
Director, Product Security
ClearPath Health
